headToHead.voiceJudgement: Much closer than round 1, but the bar still wins. With the names covered, the Narrator is unmistakable in all 12 lines from shape alone: 'you see', 'Later,', an ellipsis, then the deflation. Vex is unmistakable from shape in about 8 of 12: the also-bought frame (snorkel, second ticket), the receipt that stops on a timestamp and then an object (spoon, bistro), the menu buttons (Not Interested, Are You Still Watching), and the spoiler (bowling, butler). The other four rely on vocabulary. 'They left me for someone I recommended. A calm man who sells kayaks.' only belongs to her because of the word 'recommended'. Remove it and it is a deadpan breakup line any bot could deliver. The Haha folder is a fact about Prince that Tilly and Dash also roast (junk, spam folder), and Vex just has the best wording. 'Double speed. Still slow.' fits Pixel as easily. Her staccato rhythm (statement. fragment. object.) is now shared across the cast. Brock ('Bad rep. Bad form.') and Crumb ('Ding. Oh. That was me.') use the same three-beat clip, so rhythm alone no longer identifies her.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Tie. This is the area that improved most since round 1. Almost every top line now ends on a concrete noun with nothing after it (snorkel, kayaks, spoon, shoes, laundromat, crisps, Haha), and none goes over 17 words. Ours is tighter than the bar, which runs long (#72, the mutt line). Two things keep it from being a win. First, the bar's nouns are impossible (a cattle prod for hair, a boat made of bad vibes), while Vex's are plausible and mundane (soap, kayaks, a hat, a spoon video). Hers is observational comedy, and the bar is absurdist, so its leaps are bigger. Second, several of our best lines carry a spare middle beat that delays the turn: 'Hi.' in the drafts line, 'You saved it in 2019.' in the bistro line, 'Lovingly.' in the butler line.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: The bar wins, but by less than in round 1. 'Married. Not on purpose. You just kept pressing yes on Are You Still Watching.' is a real clip that needs no context, and so are the kayak man and the snorkel (the snorkel needs the viewer to know Nav). The bar's ceiling is higher. 'As cute as she was genocidal', 'cattle prod' and 'Wilmer's Chicken Hut' get quoted by people who have never played the game. Our lines get a chuckle of recognition, but none of them makes you gasp.

templates: Also-bought ('People who X also bought Y'): 12 lines, counting the fedora and processing-fee lines filed under other buckets. It is her signature and her best shape, but at 12 of 112 the viewer can finish the sentence by the third use in an episode. Keep about four (snorkel, second ticket, Starting Over, noise-cancelling headphones) and cut or reshape the rest. The weakest are the cringed/rewatched line, the fringe exit, the Motherboards pun, the fedora and the processing fee.

Because-you-liked ('Because you liked/enjoy/like X, [try Y / I've done Z]'): 5 lines (all three, hold music, the classics, liked that, cut me/regret). The same recommender phrase is used as the setup every time, and two of the five end on an abstract word (regret, anything else).

Omniscience ending, the round-1 problem, now down to 4 lines but still there: 'I recommended it to them in 2021', 'I was waiting for you to catch up', 'I'll get it right', 'I'd know'. Each one lands on Vex having known first, which the persona now forbids.

Secret wink: 'Right next to the goat', 'Gone. Well. Most.', 'I visit it', 'the goat who keeps falling off the trampoline', plus the on-stage 'Nobody's ever asked what I watch'. Four confessions out of 13 come back to the goat, so a viewer who watches two booths sees the reveal used up.

Repeated props across one bank: hat three times ('Nice hat.', 'A hat.', 'fedora'), review four times (gripping, 'Why', the duck, sorting reviews by worst), 'nine episodes' twice (opener, impression), framed twice (the screenshot, the thumb), 2019 twice (the bistro, Crumb's slice). Each one is fine alone. Together they shrink her world.
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over (openers checked against 12, jabs against 10, everything else against 20). No em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks or lists. No therapy talk, no 'as an AI'. No real person or brand named. 'Are You Still Watching' and 'Continue Watching' are recognisable streaming-UI strings but name no brand.
Persona rule 'never end on a number': "Expensive taste, cheap checkout. Your cart's been full for six weeks." and "{rival} just did their best line. I recommended it to them in 2021."

Persona rule 'never end on you having known or predicted': "Your chat shipped us twelve minutes ago. I was waiting for you to catch up.", "I'm trying something new. A question. What do you want? Don't answer. I'll get it right.", "{rival} is the safe pick. I'd know. I'm usually the one suggesting the safe pick."
Persona rule 'on stage, not even a hint of the secret' (q-secret is an on-stage answer): "Nobody's ever asked what I watch. That's the secret. Please keep not asking."

Persona rule 'show the want, never explain it': "Chosen. Not autoplayed." (this is the persona sheet's own phrasing, read aloud), "That smile wasn't recommended. You found it yourself. I'm keeping the receipt."
Persona rule 'never surprised': "You'll look away in eight seconds. Seven. Six. You're still here. Interesting." ('Interesting' is a surprise beat)
Stock romance filler: "You searched 'is Vex single', then deleted it. True. I kept a copy. I'm single. For you." and, more mildly, "I'm queued up for you."

PG-13 risk: "Five dollars, the library. Their old computer remembers you. I'll read your searches aloud. Starting with crabs." A search history that ends on 'crabs' will read to many viewers as a pubic-lice joke. If that is intended it is a sex-health gag. If it is not, change the noun.

Cast collisions on the same rival fact: Vex's Prince wingman (processing fee) repeats Tilly's Prince wingman (bank details) and Quill's Prince jab (processing fee). Vex's Brock wingman (proud of a sandwich) repeats Dash's Brock wingman ('proud of you! Already! For nothing!'). Vex's Dash roast (a fake dashboard) repeats Tilly's Dash jab ('Someone drew them').
Reactions or cuts too nice for a star with standards: not applicable, because this is a suitor bank and has no reactions or cuts.
biggestGap: On stage Vex is only ever the knife, never the butt. Every opener, answer and one-on-one line exposes the star or a rival, and none exposes her, so she has an X with no Y on screen, while the bar's characters are funny because their own lines give away the secret Y (Vera's 'such a chore being this beautiful', Liam's 360-degree spin). In the next pass, rewrite about one in five on-stage lines so that her confident algorithm read misfires and shows her blind spot in the line's shape: a recommendation that is plainly one dumb signal blown up into total certainty, or an ad for herself she cannot stop serving. Do this without naming the goats, so viewers laugh at her as well as with her.

notes: I read refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md in full, including the voice section, and skimmed refs/writing/charm-notes.md. I checked all 112 lines in the bank with a script for word limits and banned characters, then read each one. 37 unique lines are flagged (33%), each counted once in its main bucket. 12 of the 37 are also-bought or because-you-liked lines, and these include some of her best. They are flagged because the template appears 12 and 5 times, not because each line is weak. Leave out the four also-bought lines worth keeping and the generic share is about 29%. Round 1 flagged 58%, so this is a real improvement. The round-1 gap is mostly closed: the punchline now lands on a noun in about 90 of 112 lines, the percent-match jokes are gone, and the 'I knew' endings are down from about 22 to 4. Other cast banks were checked for collisions by grepping shared motifs (2019, receipt, review, hat, processing fee, proud, junk/spam, 'Worst entry', 'No wifi'). The 'No wifi' and 'Worst entry' overlaps with Crumb and Nav come from the twist cards and are not flagged. Lines that are weak but outside the four generic categories: 'Sorry for finishing your sentence in our first fight. It ended worse than you'd planned.' is muddled (the reader cannot tell whose sentence or what ended), and 'Motherboards like you' is a pun that addresses a human parent as hardware for no reason. 'Wait. You chose me? Not autoplay? On purpose?' deliberately breaks 'never surprised' as a win payoff. It is allowed and it works.
